description: A peak normaliser: it measures the loudest recent peak and divides the audio by it, so quiet passages come out at the same level as loud ones

params.text: Sets how long the measured peak takes to fall away in ENV, and how long each measuring window lasts in S&H; the reading is in milliseconds and the two positions of the mode switch scale it differently
Crossfades between the untouched input and the normalised signal, dry at the far left and fully normalised at the far right
Chooses how the peak is measured: ENV follows the peak and lets it fall away, S&H takes the loudest value of each measuring window and holds it until the next one
Sets a floor for the measured peak, so sound below it is not lifted; the knob reads in volts, 1V at the far right down to a two hundred and fifty sixth of a volt at the far left
Tilts the measured peak through a 20Hz filter before it is divided out: turned down the sound gets clickier, turned up it gets smoother, and far from centre the output can get very loud

inputs.text: Scales the output like a VCA, silent at 0V and full at 10V; with nothing patched the jack reads 10V

outputs.text: The normalised audio, soft clipped, with the dry signal mixed back in according to the Mix knob

notes: This module is mono. It reads only the first channel of a polyphonic cable and sends one channel out

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 10V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
